$comment: External source provenance. Hand-authored, reviewed, never regenerated from a run. This file records where the SUBSTANCE of a requirement came from and how strongly it is claimed. It is not a rule authority: no entry here carries level, severity, appliesTo, or requirement text, so it is structurally incapable of redefining a rule (ADR 0009). Standards prose may name a source only inside a structured citation token, and every token is validated against the enumerated facts below (ADR 0013). External conformance level and local enforcement level are independent axes; the levels recorded here are properties of the external criteria and no mechanism reads them.

proseGuard.$comment: Strings that may not appear in standards/*.md outside a citation token. Bare 'ARIA' is deliberately absent: it names a technology (aria-* attributes, ARIA roles) as well as a source, and prose needs the technology. The APG is guarded under its own names.

mappingRules.$comment: Constraints scripts/provenance.mjs enforces over the mappings below. They are stated here so the artifact documents its own guarantees.
mappingRules.noNormativeFields: A mapping carries standard/sourceId/criterion/citation/normativeStrength/notes and nothing else. It has no field capable of expressing level, severity, appliesTo, or requirement text (Standard 38 R4).
mappingRules.directlyAdoptedRequiresNormativeSource: Only a source with authority 'normative' may back a 'directly-adopted' mapping. An advisory or heuristic source may back 'interpreted', 'strengthened', or 'recommendation' only — a design-guidance recommendation is never a conformance requirement (Standard 38 R6).
mappingRules.retrievedSourcesOnly: A source whose retrieval.status is not 'retrieved' may not appear in any mapping (Standard 38 R7).
mappingRules.levelIsNotLevel: The conformance level recorded on a criterion is a property of that criterion. It does not determine, and is never read to determine, the local rule's level. Several criteria at the lowest external tier back rules this framework makes 'forbidden' and non-exemptible; one at the highest tier backs a 'required' rule. Both are local governance decisions (Standard 38 R5).
mappingRules.ruleMappingsAreSeparate: mappings[] is standard-keyed and is checked against the citation tokens in that standard's prose. ruleMappings[] is ruleId-keyed and records where a catalog rule's substance came from; a catalog entry carries no prose, so there is no token to check it against. The two are separate arrays because merging them would put two claims under one verification regime, and the weaker one would govern both. Both key sets exclude every rule property.
mappingRules.ruleMappingsDescribeTheCatalog: Every accessibility rule appears in ruleMappings[] or as a ruleId entry in projectAuthored[]; there is no third state. A record naming a rule the catalog does not define is a failure, so provenance describes the catalog rather than exceeding it (Standard 38 R9).

projectAuthored.rationale: The distinction between agent-invocable capability and agent-driven UI, and the rule that automation navigability never establishes accessibility conformance, are this framework's.
The repository boundary and its cross-reference mechanism are internal architecture.
Design-system strategy, proportionality, token contracts, and the conditional token-drift signal are this framework's. No retrieved source backs them.
Component reuse and state documentation. The state examples come from the source prompt, not from an external standard.
Spacing systems and the explicit prohibition on pixel policing are this framework's.
Performance as UX, including the deliberate refusal to prescribe numeric thresholds.
AI user experience. No retrieved source addresses generated-content presentation, proposal-versus-execution, or fabricated confidence.

Supported-environment declaration and the rule that unsupported environments never improve a score. The two platform design-guidance sources that would have informed the platform-convention requirements could not be retrieved and back nothing; see their retrieval records.

The Must-Never layer. Several prohibitions have accessibility subjects that appear in mappings under their owning standards; the prohibition form, the non-exemptibility, and the persuasion-versus-manipulation test are this framework's.
Design/code consistency and artifact freshness.
Artifact locations, decision recording, and the nine-question fresh-reader test.
UI definition of done.
Rule identity and catalog architecture. Internal.
Policy, applicability, and exceptions. The two-gate model comes from the owner's enforcement-architecture prompt, which is an internal source.
Evidence, assurance, and compliance output. Internal architecture.
Browser and visual evidence contract, and the committed-content freshness model. Internal.
Manual design review and the attestation model, including the gating semantics decision.
External source provenance. This standard governs the artifact it would otherwise be recorded in.
Bootstrap and reconstruction. The epistemic label vocabulary is shared with EngineeringStandards, an internal source.
Detector and testing integrity. Internal.
